cot.physical_observation: Two identical point-mass beads start at rest at A=(0,H) on a vertical wall (H=1.879 m) and slide frictionlessly under gravity (g=9.800 m/s^2) to B=(D,0) on the floor (D=2.967 m). One descends along the straight chord A->B; the other along the brachistochrone (cycloid arc). The cycloid bead reaches B first; both then rest at B.

physical_law.name: Brachistochrone problem (Bernoulli, 1696) and energy conservation on a frictionless ramp
physical_law.statement: Among smooth curves connecting two points in a uniform gravitational field, the cycloid with cusp at A minimises the time of descent of a bead released from rest. v=\sqrt(2 g h) on any frictionless wire.
physical_law.formula: Cycloid: x=R(theta-\sin theta), y=H-R(1-\cos theta); endpoint: (theta_e-\sin theta_e)/(1-\cos theta_e)=D/H, R=H/(1-\cos theta_e); theta(t)=\sqrt(g/R) t; T_brach=\sqrt(R/g) theta_e. Chord: L=\sqrt(D^2+H^2), a=g H/L, T_straight=\sqrt(2 L^2/(g H)).

state_variables: s(t): arc length along the chord (m)
equations_latex: s(t) = 0.5 \cdot (g \cdot H/L) \cdot t^2 = 0.5 \cdot 5.24417 \cdot t^2, clamp at L=3.512200
equations_python: theta (t) = np.sqrt (g/R) * t, R=0.939738, clamp * at * theta_e=3.149439
x_cyc(t) = R * ( theta - np.sin ( theta )); y_cyc(t) = H - R * (1 - np.cos ( theta ))

derivation_steps: Cycloid with cusp at A:  x=R(theta-\sin theta), y=H-R(1-\cos theta).  Endpoint constraints  R(theta_e-\sin theta_e)=D, R(1-\cos theta_e)=H  give  (theta_e-\sin theta_e)/(1-\cos theta_e)=D/H.
Numerical brentq solve: theta_e = 3.14944 rad (180.45 deg).  R = 0.93974 m.
Energy conservation along the cycloid yields (d theta/dt)^2 = g/R, so theta(t) = \sqrt(g/R) t and T_brach = \sqrt(R/g) theta_e = 0.9753 s.
Chord A->B: L = \sqrt(D^2+H^2) = 3.5122 m, \sin alpha = H/L, a = g \cdot H/L = 5.2442 m/s^2.
s(t) = (1/2) a t^2; T_straight = \sqrt(2L^2/(gH)) = 1.1574 s.  Difference Delta T = 0.1821 s, so cycloid wins.

numerical_method.solver: scipy.optimize.brentq for the cycloid endpoint equation; closed-form kinematics for both beads.
numerical_method.tolerance: brentq xtol=1e-12 on theta_e in (1e-6, 2 \cdot pi - 1e-6).
numerical_method.justification: Both motions are integrable in closed form; sampling x(t),y(t) on the time grid avoids ODE-integrator drift.

code_validation.ode_source: Cycloid endpoint equations and closed-form kinematics on chord and cycloid.
code_validation.energy_check: (1/2)(\dot{s})^2 = g(H - y) holds identically on the cycloid given theta(t)=\sqrt(g/R)t.

expected_behavior: Both beads start at A; cycloid bead reaches B at t ~ 0.975 s.
Chord bead reaches B at t ~ 1.157 s, ~0.182 s later.
After arrival, beads rest at B for the remainder of the window.
